# 2 Samuel Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 178v–179r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_010_page_001.jpg, 2SA_010_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Some time later, the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king in his place. **2** David thought, "I should show faithful love to Hanun son of Nahash, the way his father showed faithful love to me." So David sent a delegation to express sympathy over his father's death. But when David's men arrived in the land of the Ammonites, **3** the Ammonite commanders said to Hanun their lord, "Do you really believe David is trying to honor your father by sending you these men to offer condolences? He sent them to scout out the city, spy on it, and plan its overthrow!"

**4** So Hanun seized David's envoys, shaved off half of each man's beard, hacked their robes off at the waist, and sent them packing.

**5** When David was told what had happened, he sent word to meet the men — they were too humiliated to come home. The king told them, "Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, then return."

**6** The Ammonites realized they had made a stench of themselves before David, so they hired mercenaries: twenty thousand Aramean foot soldiers from Beth-rehob and Zobah, a thousand men from the king of Maacah, and twelve thousand from Tob.

**7** When David heard about it, he dispatched Joab with the entire army and the elite warriors.

**8** The Ammonites marched out and formed their battle line at the city gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah positioned themselves separately in the open country.

**9** Joab saw that he faced enemies both ahead and behind. He handpicked the best fighters in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans. **10** He placed the rest of the troops under his brother Abishai's command to face the Ammonites.

**11** He told Abishai, "If the Arameans overpower me, come rescue me. If the Ammonites overpower you, I'll come rescue you. **12** Be brave! Let's fight with everything we have — for our people and for the cities of our God. And the LORD will do what he sees as right."

**13** Joab advanced with his forces against the Arameans, and they broke and ran. **14** When the Ammonites saw the Arameans retreating, they too fled before Abishai and pulled back into the city. Joab then withdrew from the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.

**15** The Arameans, seeing that Israel had routed them, regrouped. **16** Hadadezer summoned the Aramean forces from beyond the Euphrates. They marched to Helam, with Shobach, Hadadezer's army commander, leading them.

**17** When David received the report, he mustered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and advanced to Helam. The Arameans formed up against David and engaged him in battle. **18** But the Arameans fled before Israel. David destroyed seven hundred Aramean chariots, killed forty thousand horsemen, and struck down Shobach their commander, who died on the field.

**19** When all the vassal kings under Hadadezer saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and submitted to them. After that, the Arameans never dared help the Ammonites again.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 4 — the insult:** Shaving half a beard was not just rude — it was a calculated act of political warfare. In the ancient Near East, a man's beard was his dignity. To shave it was to dehumanize him. And cutting the robes at the waist to expose them publicly — this was designed to shame David by shaming his representatives. It was an act of contempt so extreme it could only lead to war.

**Verse 6 — "made a stench of themselves":** The Hebrew *hiv'ishu* literally means "they caused themselves to stink." This vivid idiom captures the Ammonites' sudden realization that their provocation has crossed a line from which there is no diplomatic return.

**Verse 12 — Joab's finest moment:** This is Joab at his best — a pragmatic general who is also a man of faith. His speech does three things: it establishes mutual support, it appeals to national and religious loyalty, and then it surrenders the outcome to God. "The LORD will do what he sees as right" is not resignation; it is a warrior's prayer. Joab does not know if he will win. He knows only that the cause is just and the outcome belongs to God.

**Verses 15-19 — the escalation:** The battle expands from a localized conflict to an international war. Hadadezer brings in forces from "beyond the River" — the Euphrates — meaning the far reaches of the Aramean world. David's crossing of the Jordan to meet them is a mirror image: two empires colliding at Helam.

*— PNEUMA*
